title: Explain how biological homochirality could emerge and persist

concept.text: Conceptual framing: Biological homochirality is the consistent preference for one molecular handedness in particular classes of biological molecules. Molecules with opposite handedness have mirror-image arrangements that cannot be superimposed. This innovation would explain how a chemical system could develop a handedness preference, increase that preference and retain it as its chemistry becomes more complex.

The proposed explanation connects several processes: an initial imbalance or a mechanism that breaks symmetry between opposite handedness, amplification of that imbalance, transfer of the preference between connected chemical systems, and persistence through subsequent reactions. These processes need not arise from a single mechanism. The central challenge is to show that they work together in a chemically connected route, including the formation of functional polymers. Demonstrating one process would establish a component of this proposed explanation while leaving the connections to the others to be demonstrated.

significance.text: Conditional significance: A convincing connected route would explain how sustained molecular handedness can arise under specified chemical conditions. It would turn an origin-of-life question into a set of experimentally testable mechanisms and constrain which chemical pathways could support the development of consistently handed molecular systems. Its significance would come from connecting the establishment of a preference to its continued survival through useful chemistry.

Such a result could help origin-of-life research identify compatible starting mixtures, reaction sequences and environmental conditions. If the route also produced polymers with measured functions relevant to subsequent chemical evolution, it could provide a bridge to broader experimental models of life's emergence. Those downstream possibilities depend on further demonstrations; handedness alone does not establish reproduction, heredity or evolution.

An experimentally successful route would establish chemical possibility under the tested conditions. Identifying Earth's actual historical route would additionally require geological evidence and a reasoned comparison with alternatives. Explaining homochirality would also leave substantial additional requirements for constructing mirror life or developing mirror-biological medicines; neither follows directly from this achievement.

missing_breakthrough.text: Proposed technical framing: The missing capability is an experimentally connected explanation that carries a handedness preference from its origin through amplification, transfer and sustained functional chemistry. Separate successful reactions would need compatible inputs, products and operating conditions, or a demonstrated environmental sequence that connects them. Otherwise, a collection of mechanisms would leave the central integration problem open.

Concrete barriers include explaining where the initial imbalance comes from, measuring whether subsequent chemistry increases it, and showing how a preference in one molecular system affects another. Transfer requires evidence of a causal connection: observing a bias in two systems would not by itself establish that one transmitted it to the other. Persistence requires showing that later reactions retain the preference despite processes that could erase or dilute it.

The proposed route must also connect molecular bias to functional polymers and survive tests of environmental compatibility. For an executable experiment, 'plausible starting mixtures,' 'strongly biased' and 'functional' need operational definitions: specified compositions and conditions, quantitative measures of handedness, and an explicit assay of polymer activity. The supplied evidence does not establish numerical thresholds or identify a demonstrated solution to these combined barriers.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies a paper attributed to Deng, Yu and Blackmond, titled “Symmetry breaking and chiral amplification in prebiotic ligation reactions,” dated February 28, 2024, with DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07059-y. It describes the reported result as a peptide-reaction network in which an initial imbalance can be amplified and transferred. These are supplied bibliographic details and a research summary; the retained source content did not allow the review to verify the paper's identity or findings.

The retained artifact for the PubMed URL contains only a cookie-access notice. Neither an abstract nor scientific full text was available for inspection in the supplied review. Consequently, the earlier characterization of the assessment as abstract-based requires correction. The research also says publisher full text could not be opened, but the retained artifact cannot establish whether that access was attempted. It provides no inspectable experimental methods, measurements or quantitative results with which to assess the reported amplification and transfer.

If demonstrated as described, the reported peptide-network mechanism would address part of the homochirality problem. It would still require additional evidence to establish a connected route through all the proposed stages, persistence into functional polymers, or an explanation of life's historical handedness. The access limitation is not evidence that the reported result is false. The supplied material also does not establish its publication category or whether its findings are disputed.

The supplied search record is empty, so literature coverage through November 1, 2026 cannot be assessed. The source index records retrieval on November 11, 2026, but retrieval of an access notice does not establish that later advances were checked. The available material therefore supports retaining the dated research lead with explicit uncertainty, while leaving the broader present state of the field unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Establish a chemically connected route from explicitly specified, plausibly motivated starting mixtures to functional polymers with a measured handedness preference. Track the initial imbalance or symmetry-breaking event, quantify amplification, demonstrate causal transfer between relevant molecular classes, and measure retention of the preference through subsequent chemistry. Define the bias threshold and functional assay in advance and justify their relevance to the proposed route. These are proposed criteria, not established field standards.
completion_criteria.label: Connected chemistry produces functional polymers with retained handedness bias

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification: Use controls that distinguish the intended mechanism from contamination, an unrecognized external chiral influence or selective measurement. Where a deliberate initial bias is supplied, identify and quantify it rather than treating it as unexplained symmetry breaking. Report whether the mechanism selects a particular handedness or can amplify either handedness depending on starting conditions. Independently reproduce the connected sequence, including its amplification, transfer and persistence results.
completion_criteria.label: Controls and independent reproduction verify the connected handedness mechanism

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: Test environmental compatibility across a justified range of compositions, conditions and reaction sequences, and report failure conditions as well as successful ones. Explain how outputs from one stage become usable inputs for the next. Finite experiments would establish the breadth demonstrated within those boundaries, rather than literal universality. Claims that the route occurred on early Earth should remain conditional on geological evidence and comparison with competing explanations.
completion_criteria.label: Environmental testing establishes compatibility boundaries and reports failure conditions

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: BIO-02, “Demonstrate a plausible chemical transition from nonlife to evolution,” has the closest overlap. Both concern prebiotic chemical pathways. BIO-12 focuses on the establishment and persistence of molecular handedness; BIO-02's supplied title asks for the broader transition to evolution. A homochirality mechanism could contribute to that transition without demonstrating it. The roster title supports this high-level distinction, although a detailed BIO-02 definition would be needed to compare experimental requirements.

Roster-based comparison: BIO-01, “Build an autonomously reproducing cell from defined components,” concerns constructing an integrated reproducing system. BIO-12 concerns how a molecular handedness preference could arise and persist. A constructed cell could use components whose handedness was already selected, leaving the origin of that preference unexplained; conversely, a demonstrated homochirality route need not produce a cell.

Roster-based comparison: BIO-05, “Design functional enzymes to specification across reaction classes,” overlaps with the interest in functional molecular products. BIO-12 would require functional polymers as evidence that handedness can persist into useful chemistry, while BIO-05 asks for the broader ability to design enzymes with specified activities. Neither achievement entails the other.

Roster-based comparison: BIO-11, “Reconstruct the major steps in the origin of eukaryotic cells,” shares the challenge of relating experimentally plausible mechanisms to historical biological events. Its target is a different transition. For both concepts, demonstrating a possible mechanism would require additional historical evidence before identifying it as the route that actually occurred.

brief.title: An explanation for life's molecular left and right
possible: Life favours particular molecular mirror images, much as a hand is left or right. Researchers could recreate how that preference starts, grows and survives as chemistry becomes more complex, all the way to working polymers: long chains of molecular building blocks.
why: This would explain how a lasting molecular preference can arise from chemistry. Origin-of-life researchers could identify starting mixtures, reaction sequences and environments that support it.
Connecting that preference to working molecular chains would help link simple chemical reactions to experimental models of life's emergence.

sources.who: Min Deng, Jinhan Yu and Donna G. Blackmond
sources.showed: Their reactions joined amino acids, the building blocks of peptides, or short molecular chains. Joining opposite-handed building blocks helped strengthen a handedness preference in chains whose building blocks shared one handedness. The preference also spread through the reacting mixture.
sources.quote: Here, in studying a new prebiotically plausible route to proteinogenic peptides 3-5 , we discovered that the reaction favours heterochiral ligation (that is, the ligation of L monomers with D monomers).
sources.cited_for: Peptide chemistry can strengthen and transfer a molecular handedness preference.
sources.not_established: The results do not establish a complete route from the origin of a preference to its persistence in functional polymers.

sources.who: S. Furkan Ozturk, Ziwei Liu, John D. Sutherland and Dimitar D. Sasselov
sources.showed: In a preprint, the team reported that a magnetic surface favoured one handedness of a precursor to RNA, a molecule that carries genetic information. Further crystal growth produced crystals containing only one handedness.
sources.quote:
Following the initial enrichment, we then obtained
homochiral crystals of RAO after a subsequent crystallization.
sources.cited_for: Magnetic surfaces and crystal growth can establish and strengthen a handedness preference.
sources.not_established: The work does not demonstrate a connected route to functional polymers, and direct crystal growth on magnetite did not consistently favour one handedness.

sources.who: Ronald Breslow and Mindy S. Levine
sources.showed: Evaporating solutions of the amino acid phenylalanine strengthened an existing handedness preference. Crystals containing an equal mixture of mirror images separated out, leaving the liquid more strongly biased.
sources.quote:
we found that the crystals were racemic and that the solution now contained a few mg of phenylalanine with a 40% ee of the
l
component
sources.cited_for: Evaporation and crystal separation can strengthen a small initial handedness preference.
sources.not_established: The experiment starts with a preference and does not establish its origin or its survival through a connected route to functional polymers.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated parts of the route. Deng, Yu and Blackmond strengthened and transferred a preference in peptide reactions. Ozturk and colleagues reported crystals of an RNA precursor with only one handedness. Breslow and Levine strengthened an existing preference through evaporation.
missing: A connected route must carry a preference from its origin through amplification and transfer into functional polymers.
Later reactions must retain the preference rather than erase or dilute it.
The complete sequence needs independent reproduction and controls that rule out contamination or hidden outside influences.
Each stage must produce material usable by the next under compatible environmental conditions.

milestones.label: Connected chemistry produces working chains with retained handedness
milestones.explanation: A connected route would have to establish, strengthen and transfer a preference from specified, plausible starting mixtures into working polymers. This would connect the preference's origin to its survival through useful chemistry.

milestones.label: Controls and independent repetition confirm the connected mechanism
milestones.explanation: Controls and independent repetition would have to confirm the full sequence, account for any starting bias and distinguish outside influences. This would establish that the proposed mechanism produces the result reliably.

milestones.label: Environmental tests establish where the route works and fails
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to establish compatible conditions across the sequence and identify failures. This would define the route's demonstrated reach; identifying it as Earth's historical route would also require geological evidence.

uncertain: How large must a handedness preference be, and what polymer activity would count as sufficient function?
Would the connected mechanism consistently favour a particular handedness, or amplify either one depending on starting conditions?
Could geological evidence distinguish a successful laboratory route from competing explanations of what happened on early Earth?

page.title: Prebiotic emergence of biological homochirality
page.definition: A chemical route starting with equal amounts of molecular mirror images generates a preference for one handedness and carries it into functional RNA or peptide polymers. The route explains how homochirality—single handedness within a molecular class—arises and survives subsequent chemistry.

goal.need: Abiotic chemistry commonly produces 50:50 mixtures of molecular mirror images; full homochirality corresponds to 100% enantiomeric excess. Opposite-handed building blocks can stall nucleic-acid chain growth. Experiments have produced homochiral crystals of an RNA precursor, but an explanation must connect such selection to functional polymers and the propagation of handedness through subsequent reactions.

statements.quote: This project is concerned with trying to find an explanation for this ubiquitous phenomenon, a universal aspect of all life on Earth.
we really have needed a more general theory
statements.context: Blackmond contrasts an explanation of biological homochirality with proposals addressing individual molecules.

statements.body: Harvard–MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology research team
statements.quote: Achieving homochirality is essential for a high-yielding prebiotic network capable of producing functional polymers like RNA and peptides on a persistent basis.

completion.title: Independent laboratories reproduce a prebiotic route to functional homochiral polymers.
completion.criterion: Two independent laboratories demonstrate the same chemically connected route from racemic molecular precursors, containing equal amounts of both mirror images, to functional homochiral RNA or peptide polymers. Symmetry breaking, amplification and downstream transmission are experimentally linked. The polymer product has no detected opposite-handed component at stated analytical detection limits and retains its handedness through a measured catalytic or template-copying activity assay. No enantiopure biological catalyst or polymer is supplied to establish the initial preference.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no outside body was found to have published a completion test for this connected experimental capability.
completion.basis: Searches of NASA astrobiology goals, homochirality roadmaps and research frameworks, society and standards criteria, and origin-of-life prize rules found no adopted end-to-end completion test. This Atlas test operationalises the published goals of functional-polymer production, persistence and propagation, adding independent reproduction. It establishes chemical possibility under the demonstrated conditions, without identifying Earth's historical pathway.

milestones.title: A racemic biomolecular precursor acquires a measured excess of one mirror-image form.
milestones.criterion: A racemic biomolecular precursor acquires a measured excess of one enantiomer without an added enantioenriched molecular seed. Enantiomeric excess is the concentration difference divided by the sum, expressed as a percentage. On 7 June 2023, Ozturk et al. reported RAO, an RNA precursor, crystallising on magnetite with mean excesses of 38% and −32% for opposite magnetisations, using the paper's sign convention (3 and 4 runs). Nonmagnetic controls averaged 0.9% (4 runs); estimated analytical error was ±5 percentage points.
milestones.set_by: The field's symmetry-breaking research criterion, used by Ozturk et al. in 2023 and summarised by Ozturk and Sasselov in 2025; no universal minimum excess is specified.

milestones.title: Amplification brings a biomolecular precursor to 100% enantiomeric excess.
milestones.criterion: An initial enantiomeric excess is amplified to full homochirality: 100% excess, within analytical resolution. Ozturk et al. reported RAO crystals at 100% excess after a further crystallisation. As partial progress, Breslow and Levine reported phenylalanine amplification from 1% to about 90% excess by two evaporations on 22 August 2006; each table entry represents duplicate runs with duplicate analyses. These mechanisms separate material between phases; enrichment does not establish conversion of the whole starting mass.
milestones.set_by: The field's definition of full homochirality, explicitly expressed as 100% enantiomeric excess by Ozturk and Sasselov in 2025 and applied experimentally by Ozturk et al. in 2023.

milestones.title: A prebiotic reaction network transmits a reactant's chiral preference to downstream products.
milestones.criterion: A preference established in one reactant causes a corresponding preference in downstream reactants or products of a connected prebiotic reaction network. The published framework requires propagation with high fidelity but supplies no numerical fidelity cutoff. Deng, Yu and Blackmond reported amplification and transfer across a multicomponent peptide-ligation mixture on 28 February 2024 when only one component initially had unequal enantiomer concentrations. This establishes transfer within that system, rather than a complete pathway to functional polymers.
milestones.set_by: The chirality-propagation research criterion articulated by Ozturk and Sasselov in 2025 and investigated experimentally by Deng, Yu and Blackmond in 2024; its fidelity requirement has no published numerical pass mark.
milestones.threshold_quote: propagate with high fidelity across the entire prebiotic synthetic network

milestones.title: A connected route produces homochiral polymers that retain handedness during a functional assay.
milestones.criterion: A single experimentally connected route links symmetry breaking, amplification and transmission to RNA or peptide polymers with measured catalytic or template-copying activity; chirality is retained through that assay. Intermediate material passes between demonstrated stages rather than being replaced with separately prepared enantiopure feedstocks. No qualifying connected demonstration was found. Zhang et al., published on 27 October 2026, report amplification during peptide oligomerisation; their accessible abstract supplies neither numerical enantiomeric excess nor a polymer-function assay.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of NASA goals, homochirality frameworks, standards and prize criteria found no published integration test or polymer-activity threshold. This stage operationalises the research team's stated functional-polymer goal before independent reproduction.

not_found: No outside completion criterion was found for an independently reproduced, connected route from racemic precursors to functional homochiral polymers.
No generally adopted numerical cutoff was found for chirality-transfer fidelity, polymer activity or persistence duration.

results.finding: Symmetry breaking occurred in a mixture with 1 initially non-racemic component; sample size and excess were not stated.
results.detail: The text does not give a measured enantiomeric excess, and one molecular component initially had unequal enantiomer concentrations.
results.quote: Symmetry breaking, chiral amplification and chirality transfer processes occur for all reactants and products in multicomponent competitive reactions even when only one of the molecules in the complex mixture exhibits an imbalance in enantiomer concentrations (non-racemic).

results.finding: Chiral amplification occurred with 1 initially non-racemic component; sample size and final excess were not stated.
results.detail: The text reports amplification but does not establish 100% enantiomeric excess.
results.quote: Symmetry breaking, chiral amplification and chirality transfer processes occur for all reactants and products in multicomponent competitive reactions even when only one of the molecules in the complex mixture exhibits an imbalance in enantiomer concentrations (non-racemic).

results.finding: Chirality transferred among reactants and products with 1 initially non-racemic component; sample size was not stated.
results.detail: The transfer occurred in multicomponent competitive reactions; the text gives no numerical fidelity.
results.quote: Symmetry breaking, chiral amplification and chirality transfer processes occur for all reactants and products in multicomponent competitive reactions even when only one of the molecules in the complex mixture exhibits an imbalance in enantiomer concentrations (non-racemic).

results.finding: Peptide ligation provided a mechanism for enantioenrichment in homochiral chains; sample size and excess were not stated.
results.detail: The text does not report a functional assay or a connected route from an entirely racemic starting mixture through that assay.
results.quote: Although this finding seems problematic for the prebiotic emergence of homochiral L-peptides, we demonstrate, paradoxically, that this heterochiral preference provides a mechanism for enantioenrichment in homochiral chains.

results.finding: Racemic RAO crystallized on down-spin magnetite had a mean enantiomeric excess of 38% across 3 runs.
results.detail: The opposite magnetization gave a mean of −32% across 4 runs; nonmagnetic controls averaged 0.9% across 4 runs. Estimated error was ±5 percentage points.
results.quote: The ee for the down spin experiments is calculated to be 59, 36, 18 (mean = 38%).

results.finding: Enriched RAO yielded homochiral crystals, equivalent to 100% enantiomeric excess; the number of runs was not stated.
results.detail: RAO with an initial 25% excess was crystallized on up-spin magnetite. Enrichment applies to the collected crystals, not necessarily the whole starting mass.
results.quote: The 25% enriched D-RAO (red) is crystallized on up-spin magnetite and we obtained homochiral D-RAO.

results.finding: Phenylalanine solutions reached about 90% ee from 1% ee; each table entry represents duplicate runs.
results.detail: Two evaporations separated racemic crystals from the enriched solution. The reported excess fell short of 100%.
results.quote: The ee increase in solution from 1% to 90% by two simple evaporations solves the concentration amplification problem.

results.finding: Racemic NMPA solutions yielded homochiral crystalline suspensions in 72 crystallizers, corresponding to 100% solid-phase enantiomeric excess.
results.detail: Spontaneous nucleation and temperature cycling produced the excess without an added enantioenriched seed. NMPA is described as a model compound and an imine derivative of phenylglycine; the text does not establish it as a biomolecular precursor.
results.quote:
The first observation is that all crystallizers
in all nine experiments,
i.e., 72 individual crystallization processes, have reached homochirality.

results.finding: Phenylglycinamide derivative: solid-phase excess reached 100%; number of experiments not reported.
results.detail: A 4 g sample with an initial excess as low as 2–3% reached a single solid chiral state under grinding and solution-phase racemization. Purity was measured by two independent chiral HPLC methods.
results.quote:
In the presence of glass beads, which impart mechanical energy
to the system inducing continuous attrition of the crystals, we found
that the ee of the solid rises inexorably over time, evolving to a
single solid chiral state from an initial small imbalance in crystal
composition as low as 2-3% ee (see Figure 1 (left) and Supporting
Information).
